case_studies.title: AgentCheck: A Reproduce-Intervene-Mitigate Workbench for LLM Agents over MCP
case_studies.abstract: Tool-using LLM agents are mostly evaluated assuming all tools work. When a tool times out, returns a week-stale value, or has its description poisoned in deployment, the developer needs a controlled way to reproduce the failure, test a fix, and confirm the fix worked before deployment. We present AgentCheck, an open-source web workbench that turns an MCP server into an intervention surface. AgentCheck runs an agent against its real tools and records every tool response, then re-runs the agent with the response perturbed by a fault (12 types) injector. Matching tool calls are replayed from cach
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of testing and mitigating failures in large language model (LLM) agents when interacting with external tools, by building a web workbench called AgentCheck. AgentCheck simulates tool failures and allows developers to test and fix issues before deployment. The result is a more robust and reliable LLM agent system.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage LLM agents that interact with external tools, here is what to do: check if your current testing process accounts for tool failures, consider implementing AgentCheck to simulate and mitigate these failures, and review the 12 types of faults that AgentCheck can inject to ensure your system is robust.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Novel tool for debugging LLM agents. IT engineers use LLM agents in real-world applications. Could be useful in automating debugging processes or proposing a service for clients within 90 days.

case_studies.title: TerraRepair: A Tool-Grounded LLM Agent for Infrastructure-as-Code Repair
case_studies.abstract: Background: Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) scanners detect cloud misconfigurations in Terraform and other IaC languages before deployment, but repairing the flagged configurations remains largely manual. Recent Large Language Model (LLM)-based repair approaches can repair some findings, but may hallucinate unsupported constructs or suppress warnings without fixing the issue. Aims: We study whether tool grounding can improve LLM-based Terraform repair, and when a finding should be escalated because the required deploymnet-specific context is not availble. Method: We present TerraRepair, a prototy
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of manually repairing cloud misconfigurations in Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) by building TerraRepair, a tool that uses Large Language Models (LLMs) to automatically repair flagged configurations, resulting in more accurate and efficient repairs. The tool helps reduce manual work and minimizes errors. It automates the repair of IaC configurations before deployment.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage cloud infrastructure using Terraform or other IaC languages, here is what to do: review your current IaC scanning and repair process, consider integrating TerraRepair to automate repairs, and test its effectiveness in your environment. This flags a risk: if your org uses IaC scanners, check your current repair process to see if it can be improved with automated tools like TerraRepair. Check your IaC configuration files for potential misconfigurations that TerraRepair can fix.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Overall, TerraRepair offers novelty, relevance, and value for IT engineers, indicating its significance for real-world infrastructure management.

case_studies.title: A Formal Hierarchical Architecture for Agentic Orchestration with Stack-Based Execution and Lazy Discovery
case_studies.abstract: The rapid expansion of capabilities in Large Language Model (LLM) agents has exposed a critical architectural bottleneck: when agents are given access to a flat, monolithic registry of tools, the model must evaluate hundreds or thousands of options simultaneously. This leads to decision-space explosion, context window saturation, and degraded routing accuracy. To address these limitations, this paper presents a hierarchical, skill-based architecture for agentic orchestration. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of decision-space explosion in Large Language Model agents by building a hierarchical architecture for agentic orchestration, resulting in improved routing accuracy. The researchers created a tree-like structure for organizing capabilities, allowing for more efficient decision-making. This is not directly relevant to managing cloud infrastructure.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work
case_studies.score_reasoning: The paper's novel architecture for agentic orchestration is relevant to IT infrastructure and SaaS tooling, as LLM agents are being increasingly deployed. However, its immediate value in automating or proposing a service within 90 days is unclear. Low value for IT practitioners since they need clear, actionable steps to apply the research.
